message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Properties**

| Category | Property | Value / Description |
|----------|----------|---------------------|
| **Basic Atomic Data** | Atomic number | 1 |
| | Atomic mass (average) | 1.008 u |
| | Electron configuration | 1s¹ |
| | Isotopes | H‑1 (protium), H‑2 (deuterium), H‑3 (tritium) |
| | Natural abundance | Protium ≈ 99.98 %, Deuterium ≈ 0.02 %, Tritium negligible |
| **Physical Properties** | State at STP | Gas |
| | Boiling point | –252.9 °C (20.3 K) |
| | Melting point | –259.2 °C (14.0 K) |
| | Density (gas, STP) | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ |
| | Density (liquid, 20 K) | 0.0708 g cm⁻³ |
| | Molar volume (gas, STP) | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ |
| | Specific heat (gas, 25 °C) | 28.836 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Thermal conductivity (gas, 25 °C) | 0.180 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Sound speed (gas, 25 °C) | 1275 m s⁻¹ |
| **Chemical Properties** | Electronegativity (Pauling) | 2.20 |
| | First ionization energy | 13.598 eV |
| | Electron affinity | –0.754 eV |
| | Standard enthalpy of formation (H₂(g)) | 0 kJ mol⁻¹ (by definition) |
| | Standard Gibbs free energy of formation (H₂(g)) | 0 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Standard entropy (H₂(g)) | 130.68 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Oxidation states | +1 (as H⁺), –1 (as hydride H⁻) |
| | Common compounds | H₂O, H₂SO₄, HCl, NH₃, CH₄, etc. |
| | Bond dissociation energy (H–H) | 436 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Acid–base behavior | Acts as a weak acid (H⁺ donor) in aqueous solution; forms hydrides (H⁻) with metals |
| **Isotopic Variants** | Deuterium (²H) | 2.014 u, heavier, used in NMR, D₂O (“heavy water”) |
| | Tritium (³H) | 3.016 u, radioactive (β⁻ decay, half‑life ≈ 12.32 y) |
| | Isotopic effects | Deuterium substitution shifts vibrational frequencies (~√(m_H/m_D)) |
| **Reactivity & Applications** | Combustion (with O₂) | 2 H₂ + O₂ → 2 H₂O (exothermic, ΔH ≈ –286 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| | Fuel cell reaction | 2 H₂ + O₂ → 2 H₂O (electrochemical, produces electricity) |
| | Hydrogen bonding | H atoms in water form strong H‑bonds; H‑bond strength ~20 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Role in stars | Fusion of H into He powers stars (pp‑chain, CNO cycle) |
| | Industrial uses | Production of ammonia (Haber process), methanol, hydrogenation reactions, semiconductor manufacturing, rocket propellant |
| | Safety | Extremely flammable, low ignition energy (~0.02 J), wide flammability range (4–75 %) |
| **Spectroscopic Features** | Rotational spectrum (H₂) | Microwave absorption near 2.1 THz |
| | Vibrational spectrum (H₂) | Infrared absorption near 4161 cm⁻¹ (fundamental) |
| | Isotopic shifts | Deuterated species show lower vibrational frequencies (~√(m_H/m_D)) |
| **Miscellaneous** | Quantum nature | Only one electron, simplest atom; ideal for testing quantum mechanics |
| | Standard reference | Hydrogen gas (H₂) is the standard for pressure (1 atm) and temperature (273.15 K) in many thermodynamic tables |
| | Cosmological significance | Most abundant element in the universe; key to Big Bang nucleosynthesis |

---

### Quick Takeaways

- **Lightest element**: Atomic number 1, mass ~1 u.
- **Simple diatomic molecule**: H₂ is the most common form; it’s a colorless, odorless, highly flammable gas.
- **Isotopes**: Protium (stable), deuterium (stable, heavier), tritium (radioactive).
- **Key reactions**: Combustion to water, fuel‑cell electrolysis, hydrogenation of organic compounds.
- **Physical extremes**: Boils at –252.9 °C, melts at –259.2 °C; extremely low density.
- **Chemical versatility**: Forms acids, bases, salts, organometallics, and hydrides; participates in both covalent and ionic chemistry.

Feel free to ask if you’d like deeper details on any specific property or application!
